slides.headline: Standing in front of an open fridge, //[[gold]]knowing nothing[[/gold]]
slides.sub: Everything you need is right there. You still order takeout.

slides.headline: Type twelve ingredients into a recipe app
slides.body: Half a lemon. Some parsley, probably fine. Three eggs? Four? By the time you've finished typing you've stopped caring.

slides.headline: Hold your phone up and [[gold]]just talk[[/gold]]
slides.body: Argus sees what's on the shelf through your camera while you speak. No typing, no list, no wake word.

turns.text: I've got about twenty minutes. What can I do with this?
Eggs, that half lemon and the parsley — that's a herb omelette. Fifteen minutes. You'd want the butter too, back left.

slides.headline: It knows what you can't eat
slides.body: Tell it once that shellfish is out, or that you don't do dairy. It's still true next week, and the week after. You don't say it twice.

slides.headline: The whole difference
slides.before: Open app. Type ingredients. Filter for allergies. Scroll. Close app. Order food anyway.

slides.headline: It isn't recording you
slides.body: Argus only sees and hears while you're connected, and it says so before you start. No account to make. Delete everything from inside the app whenever you like.

slides.headline: Point it at your fridge tonight
slides.fineprint: Argus uses Google's Gemini Live to see and talk in real time.
